faq_draft.question: how to reduce no shows
faq_draft.answer: Send automatic reminders 24 hours and 2 hours before each visit, with a one-tap link to confirm or reschedule. Ask for a deposit on long or first-time appointments, and publish a clear cancellation window, such as 24 hours. Keep a waitlist so a freed slot gets filled, and follow up after a missed visit.

faq_draft.question: how to send appointment reminders
faq_draft.answer: Set the timing once and let the booking software send them by SMS or email, 48, 24 or 2 hours before the visit. Each reminder should give the time and the address, plus a link to confirm, cancel or reschedule. Edit the wording for each service so clients know exactly what they booked.

faq_draft.question: what is the best salon booking app
faq_draft.answer: Look for an app that lets clients book around the clock from your website, Instagram and Google, sends reminders by itself, takes deposits for long services and keeps every stylist on one calendar. Example Booking Software does all four, with plans from $19 a month for one staff member to $99 for up to 20.
faq_draft.confirm: The page doesn't compare other apps, so the answer says what to look for and what this app does. Confirm the plan prices before publishing.

faq_draft.question: how to write an appointment reminder text
faq_draft.answer: Keep it under 160 characters so it arrives as one text. Name your business, give the day and time, and end with one clear action, such as reply C to confirm or tap the link to reschedule. The post has 14 ready-made texts for salons, clinics and studios that you can copy.

faq_draft.question: what is a good cancellation policy for a salon
faq_draft.answer: Ask for 24 hours' notice, charge 50% of the service price for a late cancellation and the full price for a no-show, and show the policy at booking and in every reminder. Many salons also give regular clients one free late cancellation a year, which keeps the rule firm without losing them.

faq_draft.question: how to take deposits for appointments
faq_draft.answer: Take the deposit by card when the client books online, so the slot is held only once it is paid. 20 to 50% of the service price is common, or a fixed amount for short services. Take it off the final bill, and keep it if the client cancels inside your cancellation window.

faq_draft.question: how to set up online booking for my salon
faq_draft.answer: Add your services with their prices and durations, then set each staff member's working hours. Connect the calendar you already use so nothing is booked twice. Last, put your booking link where clients look for it: your website, your Instagram profile and your Google Business Profile.

faq_draft.question: how far in advance should you send appointment reminders
faq_draft.answer: Most businesses send two: one 24 or 48 hours before, so the client can still reschedule, and one 2 hours before as a final nudge. With the reminders feature you choose 48, 24 or 2 hours per service, by SMS or email, and every reminder carries a link to confirm or move the visit.
faq_draft.confirm: The page lists the 48, 24 and 2 hour options but doesn't say most businesses send two. Confirm or cut that clause.

faq_draft.question: can i add booking to my facebook page
faq_draft.answer: Yes. Add a Book now button to your Facebook page that opens your booking page. Clients pick a service, a staff member and a time without calling, and the booking lands in the same calendar as the ones made on your website, so there's nothing extra to manage.

faq_draft.question: Do appointment reminders reduce no-shows?
faq_draft.numbers: People Also Ask on 'how to reduce no shows'
faq_draft.answer: Yes, and they're the first tactic in the guide because they catch the clients who simply forgot. Send one 24 hours before and one 2 hours before, each with a one-tap link to confirm or reschedule, so a client who can't come frees the slot instead of leaving it empty.
